takes.heard: This shot went in, but the shot scoring system only gives it a fifty-four.
Let's break it down frame by frame and see where that number comes from.
First, pose estimation finds thirty three landmarks on the body, and object detection tracks the ball and the rim.
Each shot is split into three phases: the dip, the release, and the follow-through, and scored on ten categories.
At the bottom of the dip, the knee only bends to about 130 degrees, not deep enough, so lower body load gets 40.
On the way up, the elbow extends at over 1500 degrees per second. Extension speed gets full marks.
At release, the elbow is at 152 degrees, close to the ideal 160, so release form scores 68.
From dip to release takes zero point five five seconds. That's slow, so quick release gets just fifteen.
On the follow through, the arm pulls back as soon as the ball is gone. The elbow drops from 164 degrees into the 50s, so follow through scores zero.
Wrist loading, kinetic chain, torso control, and forward sway are all scored from the same data.
Finally, the ball drops in, and Make gets full marks.
Add up the ten weighted categories, and this shot's final score is fifty four.
Most of the points were lost on the follow through and quick release, and every deduction traces back to a specific frame and angle.
